newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN 1996 WINE EXPORTS EARNED 550 MLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN 1996 WINE EXPORTS EARNED 550 MLN RAND.

text.p: South African wine exports increased to 11.1 million cases in 1996, earning 550 million rand in foreign exchange, co-operative KWV said in its latest annual report released on Thursday.
It said that it had revised its initial estimates for wine exports in 1995 to 8.2 million cases from 7.7 million before.
The co-operative said that wine exports had "snowballed" in the past few years surging by 1,300 percent from the 855,000 cases in 1990.

"Literally hundreds of South African wines are, for example, available on the shelves in the United Kingdom. This is in sharp contrast to a few years ago when KWV wines and only a few others were available on the shelves," the co-operative said.
KWV said South African wines were exported to almost 60 countries, with the European Union being the single largest client.

On the domestic market, KWV said that since the end of 1993 the previously stagnant market for natural wine had improved. This gained momentum in 1996 and growth now appeared to be sustainable in the medium term.

The intake of unfortified wine by the wholesale trade, including exports, had grown 13.5 percent in 1996 and growth of about five percent was foreseen in the domestic market in 1997. Including exports, growth could top 10 percent.
Domestic sales grew five percent with wines in the high and medium price range growing by between five and 10 percent, largely because of increased tourism and higher domestic disposable incomes.
"This growth is, however, hampered by shortages in red wine in particular, as well as noble white cultivars, currently being experienced in the market," KWV said.
The market for standard price wines was levelling off and could fall further in future. This indicated that consumers were turning to higher priced wines and alcoholic beverages such as brandy.

KWV said the latter trend was particularly evident in its 1996 financial results, with after tax income rising to 88.3 million rand from 78.3 million rand in 1995 while net income from own transactions rose to 71.2 million rand from 47.7 million rand.
